answer.evidence: radon/raw.py:72-79 defines `_find(tokens, token, value)`. It iterates `enumerate(reversed(tokens))` to find the rightmost (token type, text) match. If nothing matches, it raises `ValueError('(token, value) pair not found')`. That answers the request directly, so A is primary. The two refs (B.txt, D.txt) say only to prioritize the file that best answers the request and give no file-specific priority. I applied that preference to A and C, the two files the refs don't name. They get 42 of the 60 minutes (A 30, C 12). B and D get 9 each as a lighter check. A grep for similar lookups (`rindex`, `reversed`, `raise`) found none in complexity.py or visitors.py. Its only hit in those files was the `ValueError` at complexity.py:41, which is about a negative complexity value and unrelated. I did not read metrics.py (C) in detail. Its 12 minutes are an allocation to confirm it has no similar lookup, not a finding. The existing test is `test_find` in radon/tests/test_raw.py:46.
